affected_use: Assume the ideal-reservoir bookkeeping specified in [A1]–[A3] of Facts & Assumptions and the adopted isolated-compound second law [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]. Then for every admitted process record of the isolated composite consisting of the system and its stated reservoir, with the pressure store included in the fixed-pressure case, $F_{T_0}$ does not increase at fixed volume, and $G_{T_0,p_0}$ does not increase at fixed pressure. If the system endpoint is on its $T=T_0$ or $(T,p)=(T_0,p_0)$ natural-variable chart, these constrained functions agree with the Helmholtz or Gibbs potentials of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]].

affected_use: [A2] The admitted reversible conversion is a record of a complete finite isolated compound with equilibrium endpoints and the additive component-entropy split required by [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]. Its components include the converted phases, the ideal thermal reservoir at fixed $T$, and every work store or auxiliary; each other component has zero endpoint entropy change. The reservoir contributes $-Q/T$ when heat $Q$ is absorbed by the system. Forward and reverse isolated records obey the second law, so reversibility of [[def-td-reversible-process]] gives zero total endpoint entropy change. These complete-compound and entropy premises are adopted model inputs.
